title: Terraform module for GPU accelerator fleet with ASG primary and Karpenter failover in Private VPC
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provisions GPU accelerator fleets in customer Private VPCs with a primary ASG-backed node pool and an automated Karpenter-backed fallback/burst pool. Motivation: production workloads require predictable baseline capacity (reserved ASG nodes for steady traffic and guaranteed GPU types) while maintaining the ability to elastically burst on spot capacity with Karpenter when demand spikes or ASG cannot provision additional nodes. The module must support upgrades with minimal disruption, health probes that gate rollouts, and lifecycle hooks for driver/AMI upgrades. Deliverables: module source, example usage, CI validation, docs for operators. Acceptance criteria are enumerated below.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables for instance_types, gpu_family, min_capacity, max_capacity, spot_percent, taint_key, and node_labels
ASG created in customer's private subnet with correct IAM role and launch template referencing approved AMIs
Karpenter provisioner created with node selectors/constraints matching ASG fallback policy; provisioner has spot fallback enabled
Upgrade path supports canary node launches with taints and automated traffic migration scripts
Health checks (kubelet + readiness + custom probe against /healthz) block rollouts if failing beyond threshold
Module passes terraform validate & unit tests in CI and example stack deploys in staging account
terraform_variables: instance_types (list) - preferred instance types for ASG, default: ["p4d.24xlarge", "p4de.24xlarge"]
gpu_family (string) - high-level GPU family label used for tagging and KMS keys, default: "A100"
spot_percent (int) - percent of desired capacity allowed as spot in Karpenter, default: 70
node_taint_key (string) - taint key applied to canary nodes to prevent scheduling until validated, default: "accelerator-canary"
max_unavailable (int) - during upgrades how many nodes can be drained at once, default: 1
launch_template_overrides (string) - JSON string to allow driver/package bootstrap variations
upgrade_strategy: Canary flow: create 1-2 tainted ASG nodes using new AMI/driver, validate health and perf using workload smoke tests, then untaint to join pool
Blue-green fallback: provision Karpenter provisioner with a new nodeTemplate; shift traffic gradually via pod disruption budgets and service weights
Automated rollback: if health checks or smoke tests fail for >5 minutes during canary, run terraform apply to revert launch template and drain canary nodes
Driver upgrades use lifecycle hooks to run node-level pre-drain script to stop in-flight work and post-update verification script
health_checks: Node kubelet Ready probe: ensure NodeReady for >120s before untainting
Pod-level readiness: example workload exposes /healthz; module includes a Job to run integration smoke tests against canary nodes
CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics: GPU utilization, OOM/kubelet restart rate, and node boot latency are tracked; thresholds defined in module variables
Terraform gating: CI job runs terraform plan and validates health-check Job succeeded in staging cluster before merging
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module changes to main and publish a tagged release
2) Deploy module into staging VPC using example stack; run full smoke tests
3) Trigger canary upgrade in one AZ with tainted nodes; run validation job (10m)
4) If successful, untaint and roll upgrade across remaining AZs with max_unavailable=1
5) Promote to production via customer runbook and monitor 30m; have rollback plan documented

operational_notes: Operators should prefer pinned AMIs managed in our AMI catalog and referenced via SSM parameter to avoid drift.
If spot capacity is heavily constrained (spot_price > 80% of on-demand), Karpenter provisioner switches to on-demand fallback per provisioner constraint in module.
Monitoring dashboards added under /dashboards/private/gpu-fleet to track availability and boot latency.
Runbook: SSH access to ASG instances requires bastion in same VPC; do not SSH into Karpenter spot nodes unless in troubleshooting mode
